metric.definition: The ratio of everything a facility draws from the grid to what its IT equipment alone consumes. A PUE of 1.5 means half again as much power goes to cooling, power conversion, and lighting as goes to the servers.

reading.body:
PUE, Power Usage Effectiveness, is the ratio of everything a facility draws from the grid to what its IT equipment alone consumes, calculated as total facility energy divided by IT equipment energy, so that a PUE of 1.5 means half again as much power goes to cooling, power conversion, and lighting as goes to the servers themselves.

It is described as the single most quoted efficiency number in the industry, exposing how much of an electric bill buys actual computing versus overhead, and it is the number regulators and sustainability reports ask for first. The theoretical floor is 1.0, and large modern hyperscale facilities report annual fleet averages near 1.1, while the industry-wide average has hovered in the mid-1.5s for years, a gap that represents a meaningful and persistent share of total data center electricity going to something other than computation.

Its siblings, DCiE, breaker-level load and peak draw, and power density per rack, are grouped under Power efficiency, and PUE functions as the anchor metric of that group, the one every other efficiency figure in the cluster ultimately relates back to.
